edits.english: And apostatized from his religion - he is disqualified from bringing an offering, as stated in 'All who slaughter' (Chullin 5b): 'from an ordinary person' excludes an apostate.

One who cast off the yoke of Torah and became accustomed to transgression. In another place (see Chullin 5a) it is derived from an inference in the verses (or, in the Rambam's language, 'from oral tradition') that an apostate cannot bring an offering, because 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination' (see Sefer HaMitzvot). And there they distinguish between one who is an apostate to the entire Torah (including an apostate to idolatry or one who publicly desecrates Shabbat) and one who is accustomed to other transgressions: if he became accustomed and was publicly known for a specific transgression, an offering is not accepted from him specifically for that transgression.
